newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures end lower,S&Ps widen losses.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures end lower,S&Ps widen losses.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended lower as fast-market conditions whipped March Standard & Poor's 500s below the 5-1/2-month low in the final minutes of trade.

Traders said declines in the Nasdaq composite, coupled with the lackluster performance of the U.S. dollar during U.S. dealings, raised concerns that investor demand for U.S. assets may be drying up as the year comes to a close.
They said March S&P 500s' last spike lower was sparked by continued profit-taking in technology stocks.
"The Nasdaq is really what started this off," one S&P futures floor analyst said.
The weakness in tech stocks battered the Nasdaq composite, sending the technology-rich index down 25 points or nearly two percent.
Several large U.S. firms each sold 1,000 contracts and one fund sold 500, as March S&Ps broke below 734.00.

Morgan Stanley's decision to cut stocks to 56 percent from 74 percent in its global portfolio may have incited several U.S. firms to aggressively sell S&P positions, floor traders said. Morgan also underweighted U.S. and European markets in the portfolio, and recommended overweightings for Japanese, Asian and emerging markets.
U.S. bond futures closed lower, also beset by worries that foreign investors may be limiting exposure to U.S. dollar-denominated assets.
There were no arbitrage buy or sell programs late in the day as index-arbitrage trading curbs were imposed on the New York Stock Exchange for the second time today.

Fair value for March Standard & Poor's 500 futures remained at 6.87 points over cash on Monday. Arbitrage buy programs were expected at about an 8.60-point premium and sell programs would have been hit at a 6.80-point premium, floor traders said.
March S&Ps fell to 725.00, below the 5-1/2-week low of 725.95, without the help of arbitrage programs. Traders said the contract hit a series of sell-stop orders.
Further support rests at 722.45, the one-third retracement level from the five-month upmove.

At settlement, March S&P 500s were off 8.65 points at 727.75, Russell 2000s fell 4.50 point to 356.00, Value Line futures were off 2.75 point to 676.00, Nikkei 225 index futures eased 95.0 to 20,355.0 and Midcap 400s eased 2.45 point to 249.60.
